_comment: Hand-verified member substitutions the miner cannot derive, each with the javap evidence that justifies it. These exist because two mining assumptions are structurally blind: a rename is only proposed when a NEW member arrives with the same descriptor, and a candidate is refused outright when several members share that descriptor. Neither can express 'this member was removed in favour of one that already existed'. Provenance is 'hand-verified' precisely so these never masquerade as derived facts, and each carries its reasoning so it can be argued with.

renames.name: setScreen
renames.evidence: 26.1 declared both setScreen and setScreenAndShow with this descriptor; 26.2 declares only setScreenAndShow. The other two (Screen)V methods in 26.2 are clearWorld, which tears a level down, and a private lambda — neither displays a screen. So the removed method's callers must move to the survivor.
renames.confidence: high, but it is a judgement rather than a proof: both methods coexisted in 26.1, so they were not identical, and setScreenAndShow may do more than setScreen did.

renames.name: allChanged
renames.evidence: 26.1 allChanged() called clearVisibleSections, SectionOcclusionGraph.waitAndReset and ViewArea.releaseAllBuffers among others. 26.2 resetLevelRenderData() calls exactly those three plus SectionRenderDispatcher.dispose — three of its four calls are shared. The other ()V methods on the class are unrelated: clearVisibleSections is a component called by both, not a replacement.
renames.confidence: good, with a real caveat: allChanged() did MORE than reset. It also rebuilt ViewArea and SectionRenderDispatcher and re-read render-distance and ambient-occlusion options, which 26.2 does elsewhere. A caller expecting a full rebuild gets only the reset half. For a mod forcing a re-render after a config change that is the relevant part, but it is not an identity.
renames.corpusEvidence: 16 corpus mods called allChanged() on 26.1; only 1 switched to any ()V on that class (clearVisibleSections), so the corpus does not settle this. The bytecode does.
